Theme

School & learning

long adjective

of a vowel or syllable

also long vowel, long syllable, lengthen a vowel, long by nature, long by position, long mark, macron

classical

Quint. 9.4.47: ūna enim syllaba longa pār est duābus brevibus
Quint. 1.7.3
Traupman 247

longus, longa, longum

declension

long (of a vowel or syllable)

A syllable is long by nature or by position: nātūrā brevis, tamen positiōne longa (Quint. 1.5.28). To lengthen a vowel or syllable is prōdūcere, to shorten it corripere (Cic. Or. 159; Quint. 1.5.18); to pronounce a vowel long, prōductē prōnūntiāre (Traupman 248; prōductē dīcere, Cic. Or. 159). A long mark is nota longa (Traupman 247).

Other words

  • prōductus, prōducta, prōductum — lengthened, long

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 159: inclitus dīcimus brevī prīmā litterā, īnsānus prōductā (Lewis & Short); Traupman 247

Examples

  • nam volucrēs mediā acūtā legam, quia, etsī nātūrā brevis, tamen positiōne longa est

    for I shall read volucrēs with the acute on the middle syllable, since though short by nature it is long by positionQuint. 1.5.28

  • sīve cum syllaba correpta prōdūcitur … seu longa corripitur

    whether a short syllable is lengthened … or a long one shortenedQuint. 1.5.18

See also short, vowel, syllable, long.
